summary.intent: Resolve merge conflicts on open PRs in the caliper repo, chiefly #434 (feat/ship-tsrs-optional-dependency), and check whether the callisto/version-packages release PR was also conflicting.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed #434's CI failure as a missing semicolon in verify-checker-install.sh (fixed in 48eff072) and found the PR conflicts in twelve files with #438. The user then asked for the conflicts to be fixed, so the worker was re-tasked to redo the merge with main winning; that result had not been reported yet. #396 was found not to be conflicting.

repo: #438 added an in-process tsrs checker and rewrote locate.rs, on_demand.rs, binding lib.rs, cli main.rs and the Storybook option docs. This supersedes #434's @tsrs optionalDependency packaging, which slice 4 of #369 would delete.

callisto/version-packages (PR #396) is owned and regenerated by the callisto-release workflow on every push to main. Do not merge main into it by hand; to clear conflicts, push to main or rerun the workflow.
A 0.19-generated release PR would not load in 0.20, so when #439 (the 0.20.0 bump) merges, #396 is regenerated again.
Slice 2 of #369 (memory and abort guards) shares rpc.rs, on_demand.rs and checker.rs with #438 and is now unblocked.

code.finding: Inside the node -p snippet, line 20 (`const libc = ... : ''`) lacked a trailing semicolon. The following backtick template literal then parsed as a tagged template call, so platform came out undefined and the script printed 'no caliper-docgen package for undefined'. Adding the `;` fixes it (prints darwin-arm64).

workflow: The `digest-mismatch: error` line in the download-artifact log only echoes the action's input. It is not a real failure, so read the actual error further down the log.
Removing a line that begins with an identifier can expose ASI hazards in neighbouring lines, especially when the next line starts with a backtick or paren.
The subagent pushed 48eff072 without running lint, check-packaging, verify-checker-install or CI, so the fix is unverified.
Destructive resolution choices, such as closing a PR or picking which design wins, were left to the user rather than made by the worker.

friction: #434's earlier merge attempt had to be aborted because the twelve conflicted files are a design conflict, not a mechanical one.
The CI failure was misleading: the digest-mismatch log line pointed away from the real cause, a self-inflicted syntax slip.
The commit 48eff072 is unsigned and has not been verified by CI.
open_items: Wait for the worker's redo of the #434 merge (main wins), then confirm lint, check-packaging and cargo check pass, that the PR is no longer conflicting, and how much of the diff survives.
If little or nothing of #434 survives, close it with the suggested `gh pr close 434` comment pointing to #438 and slice 4 of #369.
Start slice 2 of #369 (memory and abort guards) once the user says go.
Watch #396 after #439 (0.20.0 bump) merges, in case it conflicts again.
Rerun CI on #434 to verify the semicolon fix.
